units.title: Grammar I
topics: Kinds of sentences and transformation of sentences

sections.title: Kinds of sentences and transformation of sentences

summary: The verb agrees with the head noun; "with", "as well as" and "of …" phrases do not count.
Universal truths keep the present tense in indirect speech.
Indirect questions use statement order with no do.
Pick the reporting verb that matches the force of the original (ordered, requested, exclaimed).
Transformation keeps meaning exactly: only the form changes.

units.title: Grammar II
topics: Basic grammatical patterns and structures, conditional sentences
Parts of speech, active and passive voice

sections.title: Basic grammatical patterns and conditional sentences
Parts of speech, active and passive voice

summary: Match the conditional to the real or unreal time: present, future, past.
The passive is be + past participle; progressive passives use being.
A preposition is followed by a gerund, never a bare infinitive.
Learn adjective–preposition and verb–preposition pairs as collocations.
A comma cannot join two main clauses by itself.
Idioms are learnt whole; a literal reading is nearly always the wrong option.

units.title: Phonetics
summary: English has 44 phonemes in RP; a silent letter adds no sound.
Words ending in -tion, -ic, -ity stress the preceding syllable.
Two-syllable nouns take first-syllable stress, verbs second.
Weak function words reduce to schwa; content words carry sentence stress.

units.title: Comprehension
topics: Comprehension of reading passages: General and Technical English

sections.title: Comprehension of reading passages: General and Technical English

summary: Read the questions first; answer only from the passage.
The best title and main idea cover the whole passage.
Vocabulary questions are settled by context.
Technical passages: watch for numbers, definitions and cause–effect links.
NOT/EXCEPT questions: three options are in the text, the fourth is not.
